# fix-open-in-browser-redos-test-flakiness

Stabilize open_in_browser ReDoS regression coverage and repair the ineffective comment exploit input.
=== /workspace/openspec/changes/fix-open-in-browser-redos-test-flakiness/design.md ===
## Context

See `proposal.md` - Why. The current regression helper in
`tests/test_utils_response.py` builds a large `HtmlResponse`, calls
`open_in_browser`, and compares `time.process_time()` against a 0.2-second
budget. Process-wide CPU accounting can include unrelated threads in a shared
pytest process, while the tight budget leaves little room for slower
interpreters. The comment exploit input also ends with `<!---->`, which
provides a `-->` terminator and lets a vulnerable pattern complete after one
long scan.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- Preserve a regression test that fails for catastrophic backtracking in the
  old comment and `<head>` patterns, but not for ordinary execution on slow
  workers.
- Make the comment input exercise repeated failed searches rather than one
  successful match.
- Keep the change confined to test code.

**Non-Goals:**

- Changing `open_in_browser`, its public contract, or runtime dependencies.
- Reintroducing regular expressions into the implementation.
- Adding a general ReDoS-detection framework.

## Decisions

- Measure only the calling thread's CPU time and widen the acceptance budget
  enough to accommodate slow interpreters and shared CI workers. The inputs
  remain large enough that the vulnerable patterns require orders of magnitude
  more work than the safe implementation.
- Keep an absolute timing guard rather than a ratio measured at test time. A
  same-test baseline would add parsing and allocation noise, while the old
  vulnerable patterns differ from the safe line-oriented implementation by a
  much larger margin than the proposed budget.
- Remove the trailing `<!---->` terminator from the comment exploit body. The
  corrected body must contain many `<!--` starts but no `-->`, forcing the old
  `<!--.*?-->` pattern to scan from each start to the end of the input.
- Leave the `<head>` exploit body unterminated for the same reason: it must not
  introduce a cheap successful match for the old `<head(?:>|\s.*?>)` pattern.

Alternatives considered:

- Removing timing assertions entirely would make the regression test unable to
  detect a reintroduced vulnerable pattern.
- Using wall-clock time would make the test more sensitive to scheduler and
  I/O noise.
- Comparing against a vulnerable regex implementation kept in the test would
  duplicate implementation detail and still require a timing comparison.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- A too-generous threshold could miss a moderately slow implementation ->
  keep the exploit bodies large enough that the old patterns exceed multiple
  seconds, leaving the threshold well below the vulnerable runtime.
- A too-tight thread-time threshold could still flake on very slow platforms ->
  use a one-second budget and verify the measured safe runtime has a wide
  margin during implementation.
- The exploit body no longer contains a valid comment -> the test is explicitly
  a malformed-input regression case; comment-preservation behavior remains
  covered by `test_open_in_browser_preserves_html_comments`.

## Migration Plan

No deployment or data migration is required. Revert the test changes if the
new timing strategy proves unreliable on a supported platform.

## Why

The regression tests added for the `open_in_browser` ReDoS fix can report false
failures on slow or loaded CI workers, and the comment exploit input currently
contains a closing comment marker that can let a vulnerable implementation
finish after one long scan instead of exercising the pathological failure mode.
The tests therefore need to be made deterministic and effective without
changing runtime behavior.

## What Changes

- Stabilize the ReDoS timing assertion so it still distinguishes a safe
  implementation from catastrophic backtracking without depending on a tight,
  process-wide CPU-time budget.
- Correct the unterminated-comment exploit body used by
  `test_open_in_browser_redos_comment` so the vulnerable
  `<!--.*?-->`-style pattern must perform repeated failed searches.
- Keep the existing comment-preservation and `<head>` ReDoS coverage aligned
  with the corrected helper.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None. This is a test-only change and does not alter observable product
behavior.

### Modified Capabilities

None. No requirement under `openspec/specs/` changes.

## Impact

- Test code: `tests/test_utils_response.py` only.
- Runtime code, public APIs, dependencies, and user-visible behavior are
  unchanged.

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from time import process_time
from urllib.parse import urlparse

import pytest

from scrapy.http import HtmlResponse, Response, TextResponse
from scrapy.utils.python import to_bytes
from scrapy.utils.response import (
    get_base_url,
    get_meta_refresh,
    open_in_browser,
    response_status_message,
)


def _read_browser_output(burl: str) -> bytes:
    path = urlparse(burl).path
    if not path or not Path(path).exists():
        path = burl.replace("file://", "")
    return Path(path).read_bytes()


def test_open_in_browser():
    url = "http://www.example.com/some/page.html"
    body = (
        b"<html> <head> <title>test page</title> </head> <body>test body</body> </html>"
    )

    def browser_open(burl: str) -> bool:
        bbody = _read_browser_output(burl)
        assert b'<base href="' + to_bytes(url) + b'">' in bbody
        return True

    response = HtmlResponse(url, body=body)
    assert open_in_browser(response, _openfunc=browser_open), "Browser not called"

    resp = Response(url, body=body)
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        open_in_browser(resp, _openfunc=browser_open)  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_get_meta_refresh():
    r1 = HtmlResponse(
        "http://www.example.com",
        body=b"""
    <html>
    <head><title>Dummy</title><meta http-equiv="refresh" content="5;url=http://example.org/newpage" /></head>
    <body>blahablsdfsal&</body>
    </html>""",
    )
    r2 = HtmlResponse(
        "http://www.example.com",
        body=b"""
    <html>
    <head><title>Dummy</title><noScript>
    <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="5;url=http://example.org/newpage" /></head>
    </noSCRIPT>
...

    def check_base_url(burl):
        bbody = _read_browser_output(burl)
        base_tag = b'<base href="' + to_bytes(url) + b'">'
        assert bbody.count(base_tag) == 1
        index = bbody.index(base_tag)
        # The base tag is not commented out.
        assert bbody.rfind(b"<!--", 0, index) <= bbody.rfind(b"-->", 0, index)
        # The base tag comes after the doctype declaration, if any.
        assert b"<!DOCTYPE" not in bbody[index:]
        return True

    resp = HtmlResponse(url, body=body)
    assert open_in_browser(resp, _openfunc=check_base_url)


def _assert_open_in_browser_is_fast(body: bytes) -> None:
    # The exploit inputs are large enough that a vulnerable implementation
    # needs seconds to go through them, while a safe one stays in the low
    # milliseconds even on a slow interpreter.
    max_cpu_time = 0.2

    response = HtmlResponse("https://example.com", body=body)
    start_time = process_time()
    open_in_browser(response, lambda url: True)
    end_time = process_time()
    assert end_time - start_time < max_cpu_time


def test_open_in_browser_redos_comment():
    # Exploit input from
    # https://makenowjust-labs.github.io/recheck/playground/
    # for /<!--.*?-->/ (old pattern to remove comments).
    _assert_open_in_browser_is_fast(b"-><!--\x00" * 250_000 + b"->\n<!---->")


def test_open_in_browser_redos_head():
    # Exploit input from
    # https://makenowjust-labs.github.io/recheck/playground/
    # for /(<head(?:>|\s.*?>))/ (old pattern to find the head element).
    _assert_open_in_browser_is_fast(b"<head\t" * 80_000)


def test_open_in_browser_preserves_html_comments():
    url = "http://www.example.com"
    body = (
        b"<html>"
        b"<!-- preserved comment -->"
        b"<head><title>Real</title></head>"
        b"<body>content</body>"
        b"</html>"
    )

    def check(burl):
        bbody = _read_browser_output(burl)
        assert b"<!-- preserved comment -->" in bbody
        return True

    response = HtmlResponse(url, body=body)
    assert open_in_browser(response, _openfunc=check)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("base_tag", "expected_base_url"),
    [
        (b'<base href="http://real.com/">', b"http://real.com/"),
        (b'<BASE HREF="http://real.com/">', b"http://real.com/"),
        (b'<base href="/img/">', b"http://www.example.com/img/"),
        (b'<base target="_blank">', b"http://www.example.com/page.html"),
    ],
)
def test_open_in_browser_keeps_base_url_of_response(
    base_tag: bytes, expected_base_url: bytes
):
    url = "http://www.example.com/page.html"
    body = b"<html><head>" + base_tag + b"<title>T</title></head><body>hi</body></html>"

    def check(burl):
        bbody = _read_browser_output(burl)
        assert bbody.startswith(b'<base href="' + expected_base_url + b'">')
        return True

    response = HtmlResponse(url, body=body)
    assert open_in_browser(response, _openfunc=check)


def test_open_in_browser_injects_base_when_only_in_comment():
    url = "http://www.example.com"
    body = (
        b"<html>"
        b"<!-- <base href='http://other.com'> -->"
        b"<head><title>Real</title></head>"
        b"<body>content</body>"
        b"</html>"
    )

    def check(burl):
        bbody = _read_browser_output(burl)
        assert b'<base href="' + to_bytes(url) + b'">' in bbody
        return True

    response = HtmlResponse(url, body=body)
    assert open_in_browser(response, _openfunc=check)


def test_open_in_browser_injects_base_before_head_contents():
    url = "http://www.example.com"
    body = (
        b"<html>"
        b"<!--<head>comment head</head>-->"
        b"<head><title>Actual</title></head>"
        b"<body>hello</body>"
        b"</html>"
    )

    def check(burl):
        bbody = _read_browser_output(burl)
        assert bbody.count(b'<base href="' + to_bytes(url) + b'">') == 1
        base_pos = bbody.find(b'<base href="' + to_bytes(url) + b'">')
        title_pos = bbody.find(b"<title>Actual</title>")
        assert base_pos < title_pos
        return True

    response = HtmlResponse(url, body=body)
    assert open_in_browser(response, _openfunc=check)


def test_open_in_browser_text_response_uses_txt_extension():
    response = TextResponse("http://www.example.com", body=b"plain text content")

    def check(burl):
        assert burl.endswith(".txt")
        return True

    assert open_in_browser(response, _openfunc=check)

    response = Response("http://www.example.com", body=b"binary")
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        open_in_browser(response, _openfunc=lambda _: True)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
